To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present semantic correctness proofs for automatic differentiation based on a diffeological semantics and gluing constructions.

(i) we have a semantic correctness proof of forward-mode AD, (ii) we have a semantics for differentiable programs based on diffeologies, and (iii) we have a categorical gluing construction that gives a simple semantic proof of correctness of forward-mode AD.

we present a semantic correctness proof of a forward-mode AD algorithm, which uses a categorical gluing construction on a higher-order diffeological semantics, and we show how to extend the analysis to other AD methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a semantic understanding of AD methods.

the correctness of AD methods, and we provide a semantic correctness proof for a forward-mode AD implementation on a higher order functional language with algebraic datatypes.
Automatic Differentiation (AD) is a technique that computes derivatives of programs automatically, by applying

- a higher order programming language with algebraic datatypes and a forward mode AD method, - a rich semantics for higher order programming based on diffeologies, and - a semantic correctness proof of the AD method with respect to the semantics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AD method is correct with respect to a semantics for differentiable programs.
we show that AD is sound and complete with respect to the diffeological semantics.

we have given the first categorical proof of AD correctness, which is also the first semantic correctness proof, and which is also the only categorical correctness proof, which is also a logical relations proof.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AD can be understood as a macro, which is unique up to a choice of derivatives of basic operations.
we give a semantics for differentiable programs, and we prove that AD methods are sound with respect to it.
AD is a structure-preserving transformation, that it can be characterised in terms of a unique macro, and that it is correct with respect to the semantics of differentiable programming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the correctness of AD is intimately related to the categorical gluing of differentiable structures.
we can prove semantic soundness of AD methods in a way that is not only modular but also elegant, and which can be extended to other AD methods with little extra effort.
the semantics of AD can be given a categorical interpretation, and this can be used as a tool to prove correctness of AD methods, and also to reason about other AD methods.
